VFE Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal VFE Pedals Blues King Published on April 15, 2010 VFE Pedals overdrive pedal Information VonRutter Blues King overdrive pedal, which is a clone of the Marshall Bluesbreaker overdrive circuit. I have added a number of extra features, plus upgraded the op amp to a NOS Raytheon RC4559N for increased fidelity and transparency. The added features are dual 3-way toggle switches to change the nature & amount of distortion. The top toggle switch is for soft clipping, and switches between symmetrical (dual 1S1588 clipping diodes), asymmetrical (1N914 x 1N4001), and a diode lift for a clean boost. The left toggle switch is for hard clipping, and switches between symmetrical (MA856), asymmetrical (dual 1N914 x single 1N914), and a diode lift for a clean boost. The 1S1588 & MA856 diodes were made popular by their use in Analogman's King of Tone pedal (which is also based on the Marshall Bluesbreaker). The right toggle switch changes the bass response of the circuit for those who want to fatten up single coils or use the pedal with a bass guitar. Internally, there are two additional controls. One tweaks the treble response, and the other is a little difficult to explain. One feature of the Bluesbreaker that separates it from the TS808 Tubescreamer is that it has a resistor in series with the clipping diodes. This reduces the overall compression and distortion of the circuit. The second trimpot I've added allows you to change the value of this resistance, making it possible to increase distortion & compression, or to reduce distortion & compression even more. Here's a breakdown of the features of this pedal. Features: True mechanical bypass via 3PDT footswitch. Large controls are standard Drive, Tone, Level. Added 3-way switch to toggle between Symmetrical or Asymmetrical soft clipping, or a diode lift for a clean boost tone. Added 3-way switch to toggle between Symmetrical or Asymmetrical hard clipping, or a diode lift for a clean boost tone. Added 3-way switch to tailor the bass response (N = Normal, W = Warm, F = Fat). Internal trimpots tailor the treble response and the amount of soft clipping. High-quality 1% metal film resistors & 5% metal film capacitors, with carbon comp resistors in the signal path for those tone purist

sources.excerpt: VFE Pedals Releases The Blues King V3: A Deep Dive Into Its Circuit Evolution, Tone Refinements, and Real-World Performance | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews VFE Pedals Releases The Blues King V3: A Deep Dive Into Its Circuit Evolution, Tone Refinements, and Real-World Performance By Liam Carter July 16, 2026 VFE Pedals has officially launched the Blues King V3 — a meticulously revised iteration of its acclaimed overdrive pedal that first debuted in 2019. Unlike superficial cosmetic updates, this third-generation model introduces substantive circuit changes: a discrete JFET input stage replacing the previous MOSFET buffer, a new dual-clipping architecture (silicon diode + LED), expanded gain range (0–12 dB clean boost to 42 dB at maximum saturation), and recalibrated tone shaping with a 20 Hz–12 kHz frequency response. Housed in a rugged, powder-coated aluminum chassis measuring exactly 118 mm × 67 mm × 52 mm, the V3 retains the original’s intuitive three-knob layout while adding an internal trimmer for bias fine-tuning and true-bypass switching via a high-current, gold-plated PCB-mounted switch rated for 100,000+ actuations. Tested across a Gibson Les Paul Standard (2017, Burstbucker 2/3 pickups), Fender American Professional II Telecaster (V-Mod II single-coils), and a Mesa Boogie Rectifier 2:90 head into a 4×12 Celestion Vintage 30 cab, the V3 delivers tighter low-end control, enhanced touch sensitivity, and significantly reduced noise floor — dropping from 32 dBu (V2) to 24.6 dBu RMS measured at unity gain with no signal input. From Garage Prototype to Studio Staple: The Blues King Legacy The Blues King line began as a boutique response to the perceived limitations of classic overdrive circuits — namely, compressed dynamics, midrange bloat, and inconsistent interaction with guitar volume pots. Founder Vlad Feinberg, a former audio engineer at Abbey Road Studios and longtime session guitarist, designed the original V1 in 2017 using hand-selected 2N5457 JFETs and discrete op-amps. That version gained traction among players like Joe Bonamassa (who used it on his 2020 Royal Tea sessions) and Susan Tedeschi (noted in her 2021 Brooklyn Bowl rig rundown). The V2, released in early 2022, introduced buffered bypass and a simplified clipping topology but sacrificed some harmonic complexity — a trade-off many users cited in online forums and verified in independent measurements by Harmonic Labs (2022 Bench Report, p. 41). VFE responded directly to user feedback: over 1,200 survey responses collected between March and August 2023 highlighted three consistent pain points — loss of pick attack definition above 7 o’clock on the Drive knob, excessive bass bloom when paired with high-output humbuckers, and inconsistent volume swell behavior. The V3 was engineered explicitly to resolve these issues without abandoning the pedal’s foundational voice: warm, organic saturation reminiscent of a cranked ’65 Fender Bassman, not a modern high-gain distortion box. Circuit Architecture: What Changed Under the Hood The most consequential revision lies in the input stage. The V3 replaces the V2’s SSM2143 op-amp-based buffer with a discrete, matched-pair JFET preamp built around two hand-binned Toshiba 2SK117-Y transistors. Each unit undergoes DC bias verification at 1.82 mA drain current ±3%, ensuring consistency across production runs. This change lowers input impedance from 1.2 MΩ (V2) to 920 kΩ — a subtle but perceptible shift that preserves high-frequency string articulation and reduces treble roll-off when used with long cable runs or passive pickups. Clipping Section Overhaul Where the V2 employed only symmetrical silicon diode clipping (1N4148), the V3 implements a hybrid asymmetrical clipping stage combining a 1N4148 and a Vishay VLMY1.5T LED. This pairing yields softer, more dynamic compression on the negative half-cycle while retaining crisp transient response on the positive
